general.fact: NYT stars: one is good, two very good, three excellent, four extraordinary. Two stars at a cheap place is close to a rave.
Since June 2025 the NYT critics no longer hide their faces. They still book under aliases and the Times pays for every meal.
Expect 2 to 3 visits before a review. Mishan returns up to three times. Wells always did three. Platt did two or three.
Critics vary the visits: different days, different hours, different group sizes (Schneier).
Reservations come under fake names or are booked by a friend. A guest who arrives after their party may be the critic (Wells habit).
Pete Wells waited at least two months after opening before reviewing. Use that as a rough guide for when critics show up.
The tell that a NYT review is coming: the Times calls for fact-checking and to book a photographer. For Albi that came about a month after the critic was spotted.
New York magazine paused its star ratings and has not said when they return. Current reviews are prose only.
Michelin inspectors book under assumed names, eat 250+ anonymous meals a year, take no notes at the table, and pay in full.
Michelin inspectors often dine alone but copy the usual crowd. At a couples place they may come as two inspectors.
A Michelin inspector may introduce themselves only after the bill is paid, for example to ask questions.
Michelin stars need inspector agreement. Disagreement means more visits. NYC 2025 stars were announced November 18, 2025.
James Beard Best New Restaurant (2026 cycle) covered places opened Oct 1, 2025 to Sept 30, 2026. iara opened Oct 2, 2026, so it would fall in the next cycle if the window rolls forward the same way.
Best plan for staff: treat every table the same. Consistency is what every critic and inspector tests.

people.caresAbout: Imagination, ambience, service, technique, passion and deliciousness. Loves immigrant-run and hole-in-the-wall places. Judges a place for what it is, not against fine dining.
